hook.text: Epictetus said: 'It is not things that disturb us, but our judgments about things.' Envy is a judgment, not a fact.

buildup.text: Stoics practiced 'negative visualization'—imagining losing what you have—to appreciate it before envy strikes.

discovery.text: Marcus Aurelius wrote that envying others is irrational: you don't know their suffering, only their display.

twist.text: Modern CBT borrowed heavily from Stoicism. Challenging envious thoughts uses the same logic Epictetus taught.

climax.text: The Stoic aim isn't to kill emotion but to question it: 'Is this envy based on truth or on a story I'm telling myself?'

punchline.text: The Stoics didn't defeat envy. They questioned it to death.

quiz.question: What Stoic practice helps counter envy?
